title: v1/chat.completions: soft-stop matching, streaming resume and fncall continuity
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Improves /v1/chat.completions parity: introduces configurable soft-stop matching, deterministic logprob backoff for truncated streams, streaming resume checkpoints, and improved function-call continuity across stream reconnects. No public API surface breaking changes.
body:
Motivation: Customers integrating with OpenAI-style /v1/chat.completions reported two classes of reliability issues in production: (1) fragile stop-token matching when downstream truncation or tokenization differences occur, and (2) stream reconnects causing function-call (fn_call/tool) sequences to be lost or duplicated. This PR implements a compatibility layer that: (A) supports 'soft' stop matching (suffix-aware and token-boundary tolerant) with configurable sensitivity per request, (B) adds a streaming resume protocol that replays minimal context and reconciles partial deltas, and (C) preserves function-call continuity across reconnects by persisting call fragments to an ephemeral resume store and emitting deterministic end-of-call markers.

Summary of changes:
- OpenAI compat: add opt-in param v1.softmax_stop and v1.stop_tolerance to the chat param normalizer; map legacy 'stop' semantics into tolerant matching for streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Streaming runtime: introduce fragment checkpoints (streaming/fragmenter.go) and a resume API surface (streaming/resume.go) used by the gateway to resume interrupted client streams.
- Fncall continuity: persist partial fn_call payloads to an in-memory resume buffer keyed by session_id + sequence, with best-effort dedupe on resume.
- Logprobs/backoff: when stream truncation is detected we emit a synthetic final delta with deterministic logprob backoff instead of dropping probability metadata.
- SDK adapters: add small adapter changes in TS/py SDKs to surface new param names and to optionally enable resume handshake.
- Tests and docs: add integration tests that simulate staggered reconnects, tokenization mismatches, and function-call fragment loss; update compatibility docs.

Backwards compatibility: v1.softmax_stop and v1.stop_tolerance default to off/zero; existing behavior is unchanged unless the customer opts in. The streaming resume handshake is backwards-compatible: older clients will ignore the handshake field and receive the previous behavior.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime feature flag "soft_stop_resume"; will be enabled for beta customers first and rolled out to general availability after one week of monitoring.

Checklist:
- [x] Parameter mappings implemented
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] SDK adapter tests
- [x] Docs note and migration guidance
- [x] Performance baseline validated (no regression >2% p99 latency)

Related: Linear ENG-2589 (soft-stop prototype), ENG-2691 (stream resume design), SUP-4421 customer report.

review_comments: Marco Lin: High level — this addresses the core issue from SUP-4421, nice to see the resume handshake. Two questions: what's the memory bound of fncall_resume_buffer and how do we evict?
Aisha Kapoor: Response — buffer is an LRU with configurable max_entries (defaults to 5000 fragments) and TTL of 10m. Eviction is by sequence age; documented and exposed as runtime config.

Derek Chen: Requested change — make the soft-stop matcher deterministic across tokenizers; prefer implementing at token-id level instead of substring heuristics to avoid parity drift. Also add a fuzz test against GPT-like tokenizers.

Aisha Kapoor: Addressed — switched matcher to use token-bigram anchor points when tokenizer metadata available; added fuzz harness (internal/tests/fuzz/stop_fuzz.go) and unit coverage across tokenizers.
Sofia Martinez: Approve after CI: please ensure we log a metric for resumed_streams per customer so we can monitor adoption and failure rates.
Aisha Kapoor: Added metric streaming.resume_attempts and streaming.resume_success in stream_coordinator.go; updated dashboard docs.
